  "reasoning": "All 16 selected answers agree with the mathematics and their own captured worked solutions. One authored error occurs in q-181779: the solution twice labels the union of vertical lines R×N, although it is N×R. Its final diagram correctly answers the question, so there is no answer disagreement. For q-49554 and q-114054, substitutions u=3x and u=√6x give arcsec(3x)/3+C and arcsec(√6x)+C, respectively. For q-111311, a=6 and c=0.2, giving 6.2. For q-111309, b=3 and d=0.4, giving 3.4. For q-111330, a=15 and c=P(X=-1)+P(X=1)=0.35, giving 15.35. For q-111314, a=1, b=16 and d=0.6, giving 17.6. For q-110214, only X=3 contributes, giving 0.4. For q-110185, X=±1 contributes, giving 0.3. For q-181779, natural-number x-coordinates and unrestricted real y-coordinates produce full vertical lines at positive integers, using the source's convention for natural numbers. For q-181985, both intervals include their endpoints and interiors, producing the filled rectangle -1≤x≤0, -1≤y≤1. For q-65017, replacing the forcing term by zero gives the associated homogeneous equation. For q-93952, only III supplies both initial conditions at the same point. For q-74600, every linear combination of b and c has third coordinate five times its first coordinate, but 11≠5·2, so u is outside the plane. For q-74607, s=3 and t=2 satisfy all three coordinates, giving st=6. For q-109886, E[X²]=0.4+0.4+2.25+3.2=6.25. For q-126776, E[X²]=25+160+315=500. No earlier submitted answers or grades were supplied; confirmation comes from the captured worked solutions.",
